l: The Argonautica, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: Jason comes to Pelias after an oracle foretells that a man with one sandal will bring about the king’s death. Pelias sends Jason on a dangerous voyage through the mouth of Pontus and between the Cyanean rocks to seek the golden fleece. Athena guides the building of Argo, and Argus helps construct the ship. Many heroes assemble for the quest, including Heracles, and they are commonly called Minyae because many claim descent from Minyas’s daughters.

l: Jason, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: Jason crosses the wintry Anaurus and loses one sandal in the flood. He comes to Pelias during a banquet for Poseidon and the other gods, and Pelias responds to the oracle by devising a dangerous voyage for him. Jason then gathers the heroes for the quest and welcomes Orpheus to share his toils.

l: Pelias, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: Pelias hears an oracle that a man whom he sees coming from the people with one sandal will bring about his death. When Jason arrives with one sandal, Pelias devises a troubled voyage to make him lose his way at sea or among strangers.

l: Argo, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: Argo is a well-benched ship sent through the mouth of Pontus and between the Cyanean rocks in pursuit of the golden fleece. Athena guides its construction, and Argus, son of Arestor, helps build it by her counsels; it is described as the finest ship ever tested on the sea with oars.

l: golden fleece, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: The golden fleece is the object of the voyage undertaken by Jason and the assembled heroes. The expedition travels toward the land of the Colchians in pursuit of it.

l: Argus, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: Argus, son of Arestor, helps Athena construct the swift ship Argo according to her guidance. He also joins Acastus and the other heroes in the assembled host.

l: Heracles, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: Heracles answers Jason’s summons and comes to the gathering from Arcadia by way of Lyrceian Argos. He brings Hylas, who is his young companion, bearer of his arrows, and guardian of his bow.

l: Aeetes, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: Aeetes is identified as the ruler of the Colchians. Augeias greatly desires to see both the Colchian land and Aeetes himself.

l: Colchis, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: Colchis is the land of the Colchians and the destination associated with the heroes’ quest. The text says that the heroes seek the golden fleece there and contrasts the distance to Libya with the distance between the Colchians and the rising and setting sun.

l: Minyae, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: The assembled chiefs are called Minyae by the people living nearby. Many of the chiefs claim descent from the daughters of Minyas, and Jason is said to descend from Alcimede, daughter of Clymene, who was a daughter of Minyas.

l: Argonauts’ return voyage, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: Jason’s voyage is undertaken at Pelias’s command through the mouth of Pontus and between the Cyanean rocks in search of the golden fleece. It is presented as a perilous undertaking intended by Pelias to keep Jason from returning home.

l: Pelias’s oracle, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: Pelias’s oracle foretells that a hateful doom will come upon him through the man he sees arriving with one sandal. Jason fulfills the sign after crossing the Anaurus and leaving one sandal in the flood.

l: Argonaut gathering, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: The gathering brings together numerous heroes from Thessaly, Greece, and other regions, including Orpheus, Heracles, Castor, Polydeuces, the sons of Aeacus, and many others. Athena urges Tiphys to join them, and Jason leads the assembled chiefs toward the voyage.

l: golden fleece quest, The Argonautica, The Argonautica / BOOK I
s: The golden fleece quest is the expedition commanded by Pelias and undertaken by Jason with the assembled heroes. Its route leads toward the Colchian land, and the heroes’ deeds and wanderings on the journey are the subject of the poem’s opening.

l: The Argonautica, The Argonautica, Now when all things had been made ready by the thralls, all things that
s: Jason and the heroes leave Iolcos to seek the Golden Fleece in the land of Aeetes. Heracles declines leadership and persuades the heroes to choose Jason, who organizes the launch of Argo, assigns Tiphys to the helm, and leads a sacrifice to Apollo. Idmon prophesies that the heroes will return but that he will die in Asia, while Orpheus calms a quarrel by singing. After departing Pagasae, the Argonauts sail along the coast, pass Mount Pelion and other landmarks, and reach Lemnos.

l: Jason, The Argonautica, Now when all things had been made ready by the thralls, all things that
s: Jason leaves the city for the ship, comforts his grieving mother Alcimede, and asks the heroes to choose a leader. After Heracles proposes him, Jason becomes leader, organizes the launch of Argo, directs the sacrifice to Apollo, and leads the expedition from Pagasae toward Lemnos.

l: Pelias, The Argonautica, Now when all things had been made ready by the thralls, all things that
s: Pelias sends Jason and a great host of heroes to seek the Golden Fleece from Aeetes. The people question his purpose, and Jason says that his voyage is undertaken because of Pelias’s command.

l: Alcimede, The Argonautica, Now when all things had been made ready by the thralls, all things that
s: Alcimede grieves intensely at Jason’s departure and laments that Pelias’s command has brought her sorrow. She recalls Jason as her only son and mourns that Phrixus’s flight has become a source of woe.

l: Aeson, The Argonautica, Now when all things had been made ready by the thralls, all things that
s: Aeson lies on his bed in baleful old age and groans with grief at Jason’s departure. Jason is identified as Aeson’s son.
